Islands, biomes and world generations

This page explains the shape of a world: the sea and its islands, the starting island, the biomes you can find, and why a saved world keeps its own terrain.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 3 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. The endless sea and its islands
  2. 92 biomes
  3. World generations
  4. How this was checked

The endless sea and its islands

A world is an endless sea. Island groups sit in it, and open ocean separates one group from the next. Endless archipelago and the starting island

  • Small islets and palm-ringed atolls.
  • Regional and large islands.
  • Rare continent-sized landmasses.

A small islet sits at least 240 m of open water away from the main island it belongs to.

Your world begins on the starting island, at the origin (X 0, Z 0). Its terrain is gentler than the destination islands, and it is very unlikely to have a volcano.

92 biomes

A world has 92 named biomes. They range from meadows, orchards and bamboo thickets to salt flats, kelp forests, meteor fields and surface lava tubes. Every one of them can appear in a natural world. 92 biomes

The map locator can find any of the 92 biomes, so you can travel to one you have not seen yet. See the maps guide for how to set a destination.

World generations

Each world keeps the terrain rules it was made with. Worlds made with Create world use generation 10. A saved world keeps its generation when it loads, so an update does not reshape land you have already built on. World generations (terrain rule versions)

Good to know. No screen shows the generation number. The Journal's expedition section says "Landmarks appear in new generation-10 worlds" when your world is older.

A generation 1 world cannot contain meteor fields, surface lava tubes or amethyst gorges. To see them, create a new world.

How this guide was checked

Related articles

  • Maps and finding your way back: Use the compact and fullscreen maps, the biome locator, Journal places and destinations. Keep a build easy to find after a long trip.
  • Caves and geological landmarks: Some hills have a cave with one of three layouts. Rare large sites such as meteor craters, amethyst gorges and lava tubes appear on certain ground. Caves are small and bounded, not deep networks.
  • Saves and world files: A world save keeps your character, inventory, settings and every block you changed. Each world is capped at 200,000 changed blocks and 8 MiB.
  • Volcanoes, water and expedition sites: Some islands have volcanoes of solid, cooled rock. Lakes, rivers, wetlands and hot springs each have their own kind of water. New worlds have three expedition sites with a one-time supply find.
